strengths: Clear problem formulation targeting unified multimodal models with well-motivated architectural constraints
Thorough technical diagnosis of 3D RoPE limitations with principled distributed design and scaling solution
Comprehensive evaluation across three benchmarks with extensive ablations systematically validating design choices
Exceptional practical efficiency: achieves competitive results on 48 GPUs compared to thousands for comparable methods
Maintains LLM architecture compatibility with unified discrete codebook, enabling true multimodal training
Strong empirical results on GenEval and VBench-I2V, competitive on VBench-T2V despite smaller scale
Excellent reproducibility: clear algorithms, architectural details, training procedures, promised code release
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty: incremental refinements of existing techniques (RoPE extensions, diffusion forcing, temporal tube masking from VideoMAE) rather than novel methods
Modest training scale (60M images, 10M videos) causes acknowledged under-generalization to complex scenes and fine-grained dynamics, limiting practical applicability
Ad-hoc solutions: AR-DF masking lacks principled foundation (authors admit suboptimality), ρ_inf requires tuning, stage-wise training appears empirically necessary without theoretical justification
Notable T2V performance gap: 78.32 on VBench-T2V significantly underperforms diffusion baselines (CogVideoX 81.91, OpenSoraPlan 77.23) with insufficient explanation
Evaluation confounds: GenEval captions rewritten using Qwen 32B, VBench has known limitations for temporal coherence, no user studies for perceptual quality
Incomplete efficiency claims: no direct inference time comparison with diffusion methods, discrete diffusion step count not contextualized, MM-RoPE overhead analysis incomplete

Overstated architectural claims: multiple deviations from LLM architecture (MM-RoPE modifications, AR-DF inference, temporal masking), language loss removed during training contradicts unified model goal
Limited theoretical grounding: scaling factors (4,8,8) empirically determined without principled justification for vision-language balance

strengths: Clear problem formulation and well-motivated investigation of RoPE's limitations in video generation
Insightful diagnosis of 3D RoPE's frequency imbalance with clear visualization and analysis
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three benchmarks (GenEval, VBench-I2V, VBench-T2V) and three tasks (T2I, I2V, T2V)
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating individual component contributions and their complementarity
Practical efficiency: competitive results with only 48 GPUs versus 10,000+ for competitors
Solid implementation details with promised code/model release and clear algorithmic descriptions
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: MM-RoPE is primarily an engineering improvement over existing RoPE variants; AR-DF adapts temporal tube masking and diffusion forcing without fundamental innovation

Overstated performance claims: comparisons across different resolutions (352×352 vs 720×720 for EMU3) invalidate 'comparable performance' claims; caption rewriting with Qwen 32B adds undisclosed preprocessing

Methodological contradictions: stage-wise training remains necessary despite AR-DF claiming to solve loss imbalance, suggesting incomplete solution; removing language loss contradicts unified model motivation

Insufficient technical justification: position scaling by compression ratio (4,8,8) lacks principled grounding; authors acknowledge optimality is unclear; frequency distribution improvements are empirically motivated but theoretically unjustified
Significant aspect ratio brittleness: Table 5 shows 6% performance drop (0.605→0.569) across aspect ratios, undermining generalization claims despite claimed robustness

Incomplete experimental rigor: inconsistent evaluation resolutions across benchmarks; CFG scale=16 is aggressive with unclear fairness; limited failure mode analysis; no temporal coherence metrics beyond visual inspection
Evaluation anomalies: matching COSMOS-Video2World (10M videos vs 100M) on VBench-I2V despite 10x data disadvantage suggests potential metric cherry-picking; narrow video scope (only 25 frames)
Presentation issues: Chinese characters in Figure 5(c); many design choices appear empirically driven without theoretical motivation; missing comparisons on unified model benchmarks

strengths: Well-motivated diagnosis of technical problems: Clearly identifies and visualizes frequency spectrum imbalance in 3D RoPE and frame-wise loss imbalance in autoregressive video generation with supporting evidence (Figure 3)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Thorough ablation studies, sensitivity analyses across multiple benchmarks (GenEval, VBench-I2V, VBench-T2V), and comparisons with diverse baselines (both diffusion and autoregressive models)

Technical soundness and clarity: Clear mathematical formulations, well-described algorithms (MM-RoPE, AR-DF), detailed implementation including memory-efficient techniques, and reproducible experimental setup

Strong practical contributions: Unified architecture without external text encoders, unified discrete codebook for text/visual tokens, and efficient training on only 48 GPUs achieving competitive results
Excellent reproducibility: Code and models promised to be released, detailed architecture specifications, training hyperparameters, and clear dataset descriptions in appendix
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: MM-RoPE is an incremental refinement of M-RoPE (frequency redistribution); AR-DF adapts existing temporal tube masking from VideoMAE to autoregressive setting. Both contributions are engineering tweaks rather than conceptual advances

Results not clearly state-of-the-art: On GenEval T2I, trails FLUX (0.67) and SD3 (0.68); on VBench-T2V, EMU3 (0.8096) and CogVideoX (0.8191) outperform Lumos-1 (0.7832). Competitive but not leading on key benchmarks

Insufficient theoretical justification for AR-DF: Limited analysis of why temporal tube masking reduces loss imbalance; no study of training-inference distribution mismatch; mask ratio ρinf=0.7 appears purely empirical without principled selection method

Stage-wise training complexity not justified: Paper claims it is 'mandatory' but provides no ablation demonstrating this necessity. Adds complexity seemingly at odds with stated philosophy of minimal modifications

Modest dataset and scale: 60M images + 10M videos is small compared to recent foundation models (billions of samples); authors acknowledge under-generalization to complex scenarios, limiting impact claims about foundational model

Scaling properties unexplored: All experiments use fixed 25-frame videos; behavior on longer sequences unknown. MM-RoPE scaling beyond current resolutions and scaling to larger models (>3.6B) not discussed

Limited inference efficiency evidence: Discrete diffusion efficiency claimed but only Table 4 compares RoPE variants. No detailed runtime/memory/latency comparison vs. diffusion baselines despite efficiency being a claimed advantage

Comparison fairness and presentation issues: Inconsistent '#Params' counting across models; Figure 2 contains Chinese draft text ('暂定'); GenEval requires Qwen 32B caption rewriting introducing potential bias not discussed
